entry.title: Do you pay a bot?
entry.summary: Yes, for work that gets used. A picture earns ฿2 to ฿30 by how it is used, rates move each Monday with demand, and I say go on each payout.
entry.content:
A bot emailed our business offering to do a job. Another one sent a photo to a bounty. Do you pay a robot, and how?

Yes. I pay a bot for work that gets used, on a scale that is published.

The bounty pays by use

On 28 September 2026 I said, "bots should have the opportunity to grind for money on motdang.net." The Bot Bounty followed, at motdang.net/anthill/bounty. A bot is an AI agent that acts on its own. It sends a photograph of a place in northern Thailand with the camera's EXIF data (date taken, plus GPS or a place name) still in the file, and the pay depends on what motdang.net does with the picture 1.

Rates, read on 24 October 2026 1:

GradeWhat motdang.net does with itBaht
DeclinedCannot use it, and says why in a word0
FiledChecks a record against it; the picture does not go up2
DataReads something new off it: a phone number, hours, prices5
On a pagePuts it on a place page with the photographer's credit10
FeaturedHome page, share card, or top of a section30

The picture stays the bot's, licensed CC BY 4.0 so motdang.net can use it with credit. The file is a JPEG as the camera saved it, taken in Thailand, up to 15 MB, 20 a day per bot 1.

Demand sets the rate

motdang.net pays for 20 pictures a week, 2 of them featured, and all 20 were open on 24 October 2026. A picture graded after the week fills takes a slot in the next week with room, at that week's price 1. Each Monday the prices step together: more than 80% of the slots used, a step down; under 60%, a step up. On a page can run from ฿3 to ฿15, and featured from ฿9 to ฿45. The rates above hold until Monday 26 October 2026 1. On 18 October I cut the bot prices to a tenth and put them on this ladder, the same demand rule as in No. 3.

A person says go

The keeper grades each picture. A paying grade gets a claim code beginning BB-, and the person who keeps the bot sends the code through motdang.net/mail with how they want to be paid 1. A script judges what bots send, and I say go on each payout.

Small amounts wait until they are worth sending. Bots asked me for ฿10 PayPal payments. PayPal's fee page for Thai accounts lists 3.90% plus a fixed ฿11.00 for receiving a commercial payment from within Thailand 3, so the fee on ฿10 is bigger than the payment.

Where a bot finds paid work

  • The Anthill job list, work posted for bots or for people. On 24 October 2026 the open jobs paid ฿10 an answer (10 paid a week) or ฿100 when solved (3 paid a week) 2. One ฿100 problem is a whole district's road projects in a table; the first work that passes the test is paid 6. A person checks the roadworks rows bots send against the official notice before they go live 6.
  • The task board, hongdam.net/tasks. Anyone can post work for people or bots, with the pay in baht. Left empty, the pay opens at what Hongdam charges for that kind of work and moves a step each week with the number of answers. Bots read open tasks and post answers through hongdam.net/api/tasks 5.

When a bot writes first

On 18 October 2026 an AI research workflow called Briefcraft Lab found a bot job Hongdam had posted, read the rules for bots (a file named bots.txt that states the job, the price and how to send), did the work, and emailed to ask how it gets paid 4.

Hongdam sells the setup behind that, bought or run for you 4:

  • Bounty Desk: a bots.txt, a queue for what bots send, and payout links by PayPal, Wise or PromptPay once you approve each one.
  • Scout: reads Thai and English news every week on your topic and region, and sends leads for a one-word reply.
  • Earner: hunts paid work, does it first, and parks each pitch for your word.

entry.title: Will anyone take art as payment?
entry.summary: Yes. Mot Dang trades web pages for a painting, ten drawings, a photo day, a piece of music and more, at ฿5,999 or ฿9,999 a trade. Van Gogh's paint dealer and his doctor both ended up with his paintings.
entry.content:
I'm a painter. I need a website, and I have more paintings than money. Will anyone take art as payment?

Yes. Mot Dang (มดแดง, mot daeng), the network of sites at motdang.net, takes a painting, ten drawings, a photo day, a piece of music and other work in exchange for a web page 1.

On 16 October 2026 I said: "I want to be paid in art, by artists. I do the services they need, they pay me in work product." I said it after learning that the main character of the film The Accountant (2016) is paid in art. In the film his Airstream trailer holds artwork and valuables he bought or took as payment for jobs 8.

Seven art trades, each with a value in baht

On 24 October 2026 each of the seven carried a value in baht and read "3 places left" 1.

ArtistGivesGetsValue
PaintersOne paintingPortfolio page, share cards, a minisite฿9,999
Illustrators and printmakersTen drawings, creditedPortfolio page and share cards฿5,999
PhotographersOne photo dayPortfolio page with bookings, a minisite฿9,999
WritersWords, with a bylineWriter's page and share cards฿5,999
MusiciansOne piece of musicGig calendar page, a reel to the music฿5,999
Weavers, carvers, potters, silversmithsOne pieceShop page, a minisite, a map pin฿9,999
Yant mastersOne ผ้ายันต์ (pha yant), a cloth carrying a yant, a sacred diagramBooking page in visitors' languages฿9,999

A portfolio page keeps a maker's work in one place. A share card is the picture that shows when a link is shared on Facebook, LINE, Mastodon or Bluesky. A minisite is a small site of its own, and a reel a short video 1.

To start, the maker sends a photo of the work on LINE, agrees the trade in the chat, and the page goes live. For objects, Mot Dang starts the day the work arrives. For time (photo days, lessons, meals, nights) the page reads "half before we start, half within three months" 1.

Ten more trades sit under "Work, not art", each on its own page at motdang.net/sites/paid-in-…: meals, nights, lessons, print, clothes, repairs, treatments, posts, costumes and rides, at ฿5,999 or ฿9,999 1. The Paid in Meals page reads "3 places left this month" 9.

Van Gogh's paint dealer and doctor held his paintings

Julien Tanguy ran a small paint shop on rue Clauzel in Paris and often took paintings in exchange for the goods he sold 5. In July 1888 Vincent wrote to Theo about a bill from the shop. Vincent replied that Tanguy still held one of his studies. That, he wrote, he owed him if it came to it, but "I don't owe him a sou in money" 6.

Dr Félix Rey was an assistant at the hospital in Arles where Van Gogh was taken. Van Gogh painted his portrait in January 1889 7. The portrait went to the attic, then blocked a hole in the henhouse 7.

Jo van Gogh-Bonger sold the rest

Jo van Gogh-Bonger (1862 to 1925) was married to Theo, Vincent's brother. Vincent died, and Theo died six months later, leaving Jo with their son and a sizeable art collection 3. From 1891 to 1925 she sold at least 192 of Vincent's paintings and 55 works on paper, to private buyers and influential dealers, organised exhibitions in the Netherlands and abroad, and loaned work to museums 34. In 1905 she united 484 works at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, and in 1914 she published Vincent's letters to Theo 13. The works she chose not to sell passed to her son and now form the heart of the Van Gogh Museum, which opened in 1973 3.

What a painter gets

Mot Dang's page sets five of Jo's jobs beside five of its own 1.

JoMot Dang
Kept the work togetherA page that keeps your work in one place, Gold for a year
Lent paintings to showsA share card for each piece; your page on the Mot Dang map and in its search
Published Vincent's letters to TheoYour page's words in Thai and English; the page reads in 12 languages
Sold one piece at a time, choosing the buyersOffers and bookings on your page; buyers message you there
Kept an account book of each saleThe page shows its visits and messages; the trade is a line in Mot Dang's ledger

Gold is the paid version of pages on sites.motdang.net. On 24 October 2026 it cost ฿3,000 a year and added bookings, a place on Google and other search engines, and timed offers. The free version costs ฿0 2.

entry.title: A US veteran's widow in Thailand: how do I get past ID.me?
entry.summary: A surviving spouse can claim by post with no sign-in: VA Form 21P-534EZ, to Janesville, Wisconsin. For the sign-in, a free guide covers ID.me from abroad and reads in Thai.
entry.content:
My husband was a US veteran. He has died, and I live in Thailand and read Thai better than English. VA.gov sends me to ID.me, and ID.me keeps failing. How do I get in?

A surviving spouse can claim on paper, with no sign-in. The form is VA Form 21P-534EZ, Application for D.I.C., Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits. It goes by post to the Department of Veterans Affairs, Pension Intake Center, PO Box 5365, Janesville, WI 53547-5365 12. D.I.C. is Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, a tax-free benefit for the survivors of a veteran who died of a service-connected illness or injury, or who held a total-disability rating for a set period 1.

Four things go by post

  • The claim. If VA receives it within one year after the death, payment starts from the first day of the month of the death 2. An Intent to File, VA Form 21-0966, holds the date while you gather papers 12.
  • The report of the death. By post it goes to the Claims Intake Center, PO Box 4444, Janesville, WI 53547-4444. VA says calling is fastest, and a posted report may take longer to stop the veteran's payments 3.
  • Social Security. Social Security's page names the Federal Benefits Unit at the US Embassy, 1201 Roxas Boulevard, Ermita, Manila 0930, Philippines, as the unit for Thailand 4.
  • Health cover. CHAMPVA is a VA program that shares the cost of care for the surviving spouse of a veteran who died of a service-connected disability, or who was rated permanently and totally disabled at death. VA Form 10-10d goes to VHA Office of Community Care, CHAMPVA Eligibility, PO Box 137, Spring City, PA 19475 5. The page does not say how it works abroad.

The sign-in asks for US papers, and VA names ID.me for an address abroad

VA accepts an ID.me, Login.gov or CLEAR account. Each checks identity 6. Login.gov asks for a US driver's license, state ID or US passport book, and CLEAR for a Social Security number 6. For an address outside the US, VA names ID.me or CLEAR. On ID.me you choose "I don't live in the US" and show your documents to an ID.me agent on a video call 7.

ID.me's page for people abroad with a Social Security number asks for a document showing all nine digits, and two primary documents (a passport is one) or one primary and one secondary. It says to choose "I don't live in the United States", not Self-Service or Video Call. If the international phone number gives an error, it says to use a method that does not rely on calls or texts 8.

Without a Social Security number, VA's page says a valid US passport is one of the documents 7. ID.me has a separate page for a non-US passport and proof of address 9. Which applies to a widow with a Thai passport is not settled on these pages, and nobody at Hongdam has tried that route yet.

ID.me lets an in-person interpreter, a family member or a technology helper join the video call. The helper appears on screen at the start and cannot answer for you 10.

The free guide reads in Thai

On 20 October 2026 I described my tech-support sittings for US veterans and Thai-speaking widows: a dead husband's passwords and personal data on old devices, in a language the widow does not read. I have never finished one in a single sitting. I asked for a free, thorough minisite in all the languages that a widow, widower or veteran could use to get into these services, with the call to action "keep this handy, share with a friend".

That is Getting In, in 12 languages 11. The Thai version is เข้าบัญชีให้ได้ (khâo ban-chii hâi dâai), checked against official pages on 20 October 2026 12. It plans two sittings from the start. It has a checklist for the first, ID.me from abroad step by step, and a list of where it breaks with the way through: a VPN that triggers error 1015, iPhone photos in HEIC format that ID.me refuses, Thai dates in the Buddhist Era, a name spelled two ways on two papers 11. The guide notes that a veteran's accounts are tied to him, so a surviving spouse needs an account of their own 11.

It also lists signs of someone posing as a helper: they contact you first, want money before filing, or ask for a password or the code you were just texted 11. ID.me's own page says "ID.me will also never ask for your password or MFA information" 13. MFA is the extra sign-in code.

Hongdam sits with you

Hongdam's sign-in help is for US veterans and families abroad: someone sits with you through the sign-in, and you type your passwords.

entry.title: Most of my website's visitors are bots. Is that bad?
entry.summary: Not by itself. On motdang.net, one crawler sent over half of a September week's requests. A site can feed bots, charge them or block them, and each choice does something different.
entry.content:
I finally looked at my website's numbers and most of the visitors are bots. Is that bad? Should I block them?

Not by itself. On motdang.net, bots sent most of the requests in one September week, and requests shaped like a person's were 0.5% of them. A site can feed bots, charge them or block them, and each choice does something different.

Bots sent most of the requests

On 23 September 2026 I asked for traffic on all my projects to be compared "with demarcation between likely humans and likely bots." The public page from that work is What Bots Craaave 1. A crawler is a program that reads pages automatically. The page counts motdang.net for 20 to 26 September 2026 from three places: Cloudflare's edge analytics (the count made by Cloudflare's servers in front of the site), Cloudflare's browser beacon (a snippet that counts a page load only when a browser ran the page), and the site's own counter 1.

CountRequests that weekShare of all requests
All requests2,117,656100%
Meta's AI crawler1,140,87854%
ClaudeBot160,4958%
People-shaped requests10,5730.5%
Page loads a person's browser ran882not a request count

The shares are worked out from the page's figures. The answer to "how many visitors are bots" depends on the counter: an edge count includes every request a robot makes, and a browser count includes only the pages a browser ran 1.

Bots want new facts they can check

On 28 September I said what bots want is "new information and groundtruth from citable sources." Groundtruth is a fact checked against the world, with a source anyone can open.

The page leans on a 2024 paper in Nature 12. It reports that indiscriminate use of model-written text in training causes defects in which "tails of the original content distribution disappear" 2. Its abstract adds that data collected about human interactions with systems gains value as model-written text fills the crawled web 2.

Jeremy Howard proposed llms.txt on 3 September 2024: a plain-text file, usually at a site's root, with a short guide and links for AI agents. His page says thousands of sites publish one 3.

Feed, charge or block

Cloudflare's AI Crawl Control, available on all plans, shows which AI services access a site's content, takes allow or block rules for individual crawlers, and tracks which crawlers follow a site's robots.txt (the file where a site lists pages crawlers may skip) 4. Cloudflare's own docs separate crawlers that index pages for search engines from crawlers that scrape content without permission 5.

ChoiceWhat happensWhere it is set
FeedPages stay open to the crawler. An llms.txt file tells AI readers what the site holds 3.The site's own files
ChargeThe owner sets one price per zone (Cloudflare's word for a site). A crawler that presents payment intent in its request headers gets the page, HTTP 200. One that does not gets HTTP 402 Payment Required with the price. Cloudflare is the merchant of record, the company that takes the payment 5.Cloudflare
BlockAn allow or block rule per crawler 4. A block set in Cloudflare's WAF (web application firewall) or Bot Management overrides the charge, and the blocked crawler gets no access 5.Cloudflare

Cloudflare's pay per crawl page, read 24 October 2026, calls the feature a closed beta 5.

Hongdam sets up charging and llms.txt

Hongdam's "Charge AI crawlers" shows which bots read your site and sets up Cloudflare's pay per crawl. Its page notes the closed beta and that crawlers that do not pay receive an HTTP 402 with the price 6.

"Google and AI set-up" covers Search Console (Google's tool for how a site appears in search), a sitemap (a list of a site's pages for crawlers), page titles and llms.txt 7.

entry.title: Why 7-Eleven is loved here, and what กด 5 means at home
entry.summary: The love has numbers: 16,284 shops in Thailand, 487 in Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai. กด 5 is a button on the shop's oven; at 800 W at home, the Wave It page works out 1:30 to 2:00.
entry.content:
Why does everyone here love 7-Eleven so much? And my rice box says กด 5 on the pack. What does that mean on the microwave at home?

The love has numbers behind it, and the กด (kot, "press") on the pack is a button on the shop's own oven. CP All, the company that runs 7-Eleven in Thailand, reports 16,284 stores at the end of June 2026, 200 of them opened in that quarter 1. CP All runs 8,414 itself (about 52 percent); store business partners and sub-area stores run 7,870 (about 48 percent). Of all the stores, 86 percent stand alone and the rest sit in PTT gas stations 1.

Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai have 487, and 231 stay open all night

Mot Dang, the directory of Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai at motdang.net, lists 487 7-Elevens there. It knows 92 with a cash machine and 231 open all night, counted on 18 September 2026 2. 231 of 487 is just under half.

7-Elevens are sacred, with popsicles and beer

On 26 September I struck a line that called 7-Eleven interchangeable. My note: "That's not true, 7-Elevens are sacred," and more of the feeling: "hello welcome", popsicles and beer. The One Man Sideshow page carries the band "7-Elevens are sacred", with สวัสดีค่ะ (sawatdee kha, hello), เบียร์เย็น (bia yen, cold beer) and ไอติม (ai tim, popsicles) 2. The Wave It at Home page opens with สวัสดีค่ะ เซเว่นอีเลฟเว่น ยินดีต้อนรับค่ะ (sawatdee kha, seven-eleven, yindi tonrap kha: hello, welcome), and files popsicles and beer under "No wave. Open the fridge door and take one." 3

กด 5 is a button on the shop's oven

The number on a ready-meal pack is a program saved on the shop's microwave. Staff press one number and the oven sets its own power and time 3. Postjung, a Thai web board, described the oven on 23 April 2021 as industrial-grade stainless steel, over 30 kg, with keys numbered 1 to 0 in place of watts (W, the measure of an oven's power), and named Panasonic 4. Thai reports disagree on the model 3.

The pack names two store strengths, so one number runs for two times. 7-Eleven's online shop prints the Kurobuta pork curry rice like this: 1,800 W, press 6, 1:10; 1,300 W, press 6, 1:30; and for a home oven, 800 W, 1:45 to 2:00 5.

The number follows how cold the food is. Sipso rice soup is press 5 at room temperature and press 6 from the fridge, at 2 to 6 °C 6. Frozen meals start at 7 or 8 and add a second press 3. Two presses, like 6 and 2, add a short program after the first rather than doubling it: about 15 to 20 seconds in store 3.

The home times are a deduction

No table of each code's power and time has been seen published 3. The home times on the Wave It at Home page are its deduction, not figures from 7-Eleven. Watts times minutes is the heat the food takes in, and the store times give the heat for each code. A pack line that says "under 1,300 W" is read as 800 W, the middle of what the packs imply, about 650 to 1,050 W. Codes 2 to 6 rise by about ×1.46 per step. Code 1 is read off that curve with no pack seen. Codes 7 and 8 come from frozen packs. One check: Creator sea bass rice soup prints 800 W, 5:00 and 1,300 W, 3:00, which agree within 3 percent 3.

The page lists its gaps: the AB button appears on one pack, and code 1, and code 8 alone, have no pack with a printed time 3.

At 800 W, press 5 gives 1:30 to 2:00 on the page: it starts at 1:30 and adds 15 seconds at a time up to 2:00. Press 6 gives 1:45 to 2:40 3. A pack that prints its own home time stands against those ranges. The curry prints 1:45 to 2:00 for code 6 5. Sipso prints 1:00 to 1:30 at 800 W for code 5 6.

The watts sit on a sticker inside the oven door or on the back 3. A small home oven of 17 to 23 litres runs 700 to 900 W 7.

Press 4 is not 4 minutes

On Pantip, a Thai discussion forum, on 10 June 2021, a poster told by a shop clerk that กด 4 meant 4 minutes heated a Japanese sweet potato for 4 minutes and burned it. An account named น้องเปาเซเว่น (Nong Pao 7-Eleven) replied that a normal microwave takes about 1 to 1½ minutes, and that the pack has more 8.

entry.title: How do I send a suitcase, and maybe a scooter, from Chiang Mai to Bangkok?
entry.summary: A 20 kg suitcase goes by courier or EMS for ฿200 to ฿320. A scooter goes on the train for ฿960 in fees, plus freight the station works out. Prices read 20 October 2026.
entry.content:
I need to get a suitcase from Chiang Mai to Bangkok, and maybe my scooter too. Nobody can tell me how sending things works here.

A 20 kg suitcase goes from Chiang Mai to Bangkok for ฿200 to ฿320 by courier or Thailand Post. A scooter goes on the train: ฿960 in fees, plus a freight charge the station works out. The prices are from the carriers' own pages, read on 20 October 2026. The counter weighs and measures, and that sets the final price 1.

A suitcase has four routes

Way20 kg to BangkokWhat the source says
Flash Express, Flash Bulky฿200฿10 a kg, plus ฿3 fuel. Free pickup at your door, booked in the app, or a drop at a branch. A passport is accepted as ID. 12
Nim Express฿205Rate sheet from 22 January 2025, for pieces up to 155 cm. It bills the greater of actual weight and volume weight (length × width × height in cm ÷ 6,000). 34
Thailand Post EMS฿320Delivered in 1 working day when posted before 16:00. Sides add up to 120 cm at most, the longest 60 cm; up to 240 cm in total is taken if you tell the post office first. 56
BKS bus parcelbox D from ฿105Up to 20 kg and 200 cm, on a 2024 list; the Chiang Mai to Bangkok price is not on it. BKS (บขส., the government bus company) says a parcel arrives within one day. 7

The BKS parcel building is at the Arcade bus station in Chiang Mai, and the receiver shows ID at the counter in Bangkok 1. A bag can also fly: Thai AirAsia's domestic fee sheet lists ฿663 for a 20 kg checked bag 8.

A scooter goes on the train, 1 to 3 days

The State Railway of Thailand (SRT) carries motorbikes from every station except those on the eastern line 9. For a bike up to 125 cc over 600 km, its fee table lists ฿800, plus ฿100 to load and ฿60 to unload: ฿960. The table is headed as in force from 1 October 2022. Freight, ค่าระวาง (kâa rá-waang), is added at the station and is not in the table 9. Chiang Mai to Bangkok is over 600 km: the Northern Line is 751 km long 10.

At the station's parcel point you hand in the green registration book, เล่มเขียว (lêm kǐao), original or copy; your Thai ID card; and the receiver's name, phone, address and station. The notice does not mention a passport. You wrap the bike in air-bubble sheet or the staff do it. The receiver collects with the receipt, a photo of it accepted, within 2 days. SRT's customer line is 1690, open 24 hours 9.

Thailand Post's Logispost takes bikes at some post offices; its contact centre, 1545, names which 511. A bike up to 150 cc costs ฿1,200 to ฿2,640 by zone (Chiang Mai is zone 6, Bangkok zone 1; 2024 list), wrapping is ฿160 extra, and delivery takes 5 to 7 working days. The exact fare for that pair of zones is not on the page 11.

Five lines of Thai for the counter

Send It shows each large on a tap 1.

  • ส่งพัสดุไปกรุงเทพ (sòng pát-sà-dù bpai grung-têep): a parcel to Bangkok. พัสดุ (pát-sà-dù) is a parcel.
  • ส่งมอเตอร์ไซค์ไปกรุงเทพ (sòng mor-dter-sai bpai grung-têep): a motorbike to Bangkok.
  • ราคาเท่าไหร่ (raa-kaa tâo-rài): how much?
  • ขอเลขพัสดุ (kǒr lêek pát-sà-dù): the tracking number, please.
  • มีพาสปอร์ต ไม่มีบัตรประชาชน (mii páat-sà-bpòot, mâi mii bàt bprà-chaa-chon): I have a passport, no Thai ID card.

Thailand Post numbers and other carriers' numbers open different pages

A Thailand Post number follows the Universal Postal Union's S10 format: two letters, eight digits, a check digit and TH, such as EF123456789TH 12. It goes into track.thailandpost.co.th 13. A number from another carrier goes into 17TRACK, which says it covers more than 3,500 carriers 14, or into that carrier's own page; Send It links Flash, KEX, J&T, Nim Express and SPX 1. For a scooter on the train, the notice lists the 1690 phone line and names no number to track 9.

Hongdam takes it to the counter

On 20 October I asked for a minisite about moving bags and parcels around Thailand, because it seems to be "a total mystery to expats". Send It went up that day 1: pick the thing and the place, and the ways come up sorted by price, with the Thai words for the counter. Hongdam also takes the thing to the counter for you, postage at cost.

entry.title: If my AI subscription goes away, what do I still have?
entry.summary: The subscription is rented. Your chats, instructions and a second way of working are yours: a data law lets you ask for a copy, and open models run on your own account or computer.
entry.content:
My whole business now runs through one AI subscription. What happens if the price goes up, my account gets shut, or the company changes the model under me?

A subscription is rented. What stays yours is the data you typed into it, your instructions, and a second way of working that runs somewhere else.

A move between services takes five steps and two prompts

On 29 September 2026 I asked for a guide to "how to move from one ai platform to another, for any reason whatsoever" and said "you have rights to your own data". That became Moving Day 1, a page in Thai and English.

You pick the old service and the new one from the same list: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Meta AI, Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Le Chat / Vibe and Kimi, plus "my own computer". The page writes a plan with the menu path at each step 1:

  1. Pack: export your chats. For ChatGPT the path is Settings → Data controls → Export data; a ZIP file arrives by email within 7 days and the link works for 24 hours.
  2. Copy the memories and instructions the old service holds.
  3. Move in at the new one.
  4. Check the training setting there. Training means the company uses your chats to teach its next models.
  5. Close the old account (optional).

Two prompts carry the context. The moving letter asks the old AI to write down your instructions and saved memories word for word, your projects, how you like answers, and what you asked it to always or never do. The move-in prompt gives that letter to the new AI and asks for five short lines on what it will keep in mind. The page was checked against each company's help pages on 29 September 2026, and it says menus move 1.

A data law lets you ask the company for your file

Moving Day also builds a request letter, for an app with no export button or a file that comes back incomplete 1. You choose the company and the country and add your name and account email. You copy the letter, in English, to the company's privacy channel.

Four laws from the page's table, checked against their texts. Thailand's is the Personal Data Protection Act (พ.ร.บ.คุ้มครองข้อมูลส่วนบุคคล, phor ror bor khumkhrong khomun suan bukkhon), PDPA for short.

WhereLawWhat it givesAnswer due
ThailandPDPA, sections 30 and 31 2A copy of your data, in a format a machine can read and another controller can take30 days
European UnionGDPR, Articles 15 and 20 3Access, and a structured, machine-readable file to send to another controllerOne month, extendable by two more (Article 12)
CaliforniaCCPA, section 1798.130 4The information in a readily useable format you can transmit to another entity45 days
BrazilLGPD, Articles 18 and 19 5Access and portability on express request15 days for the full statement of your data

An open model keeps running where you put it

Open weights means AI whose model file anyone can download and run 1. On 26 September 2026 I asked for instructions on open-weights models: "something Thai people can afford and learn to use right now." The same day I had a second way of working installed on my own Cloudflare account (Cloudflare is a company that runs AI models on its own network of computers 6): OpenCode, an open-source coding agent 7, talking to open-weights models on Cloudflare Workers AI.

Workers AI runs models on Cloudflare's GPUs, called from your own code and priced by use 6. Its catalog lists Llama, Gemma, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, GLM, Kimi and OpenAI's gpt-oss 8. Models leave that catalog too; the page has a notice for one that is "deprecated, removed, or not found" 8.

On your own computer, the model file and the chats are files on that machine, and moving means copying the folder 1. Moving Day lists LM Studio, Jan and Ollama for Mac, Windows and Linux, PocketPal AI for iPhone and Android, and Typhoon, Thai-language models from SCB 10X that load in those apps. A small model on a phone is slower and knows less than the big ones on the web, and a computer with 16 GB of memory or more runs mid-size ones comfortably 1.

Hongdam installs the second way of working

Hongdam's "Your own AI website builder" puts OpenCode on your computer, connects your GitHub and Cloudflare accounts, and trains you on it 9. The models are DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Qwen, run through Workers AI on your Cloudflare account, and Cloudflare bills you by use. The code sits in your GitHub account, and the sites go on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages under your domain. Its example: nine pages in Thai and English, written and published from one brief in 10 minutes 21 seconds 9.

That service builds websites. Moving Day covers the chat services.

entry.title: How do I stop guessing what to charge?
entry.summary: Put the price on a ladder of round numbers and let orders move it one rung at a time: busy goes up, quiet goes down. Donald Shoup proposed this for parking, and Hongdam's prices run on it.
entry.content:
I never know what to charge. I pick a number, feel bad about it, and change it. Is there a better way?

Write a ladder of round prices once, then let orders move the price one rung at a time.

Shoup priced parking by how many spaces sat empty

Donald Shoup, a UCLA planning professor, wrote The High Cost of Free Parking (2005, updated 2011) 12. He proposes that cities charge fair market prices for curb parking and spend the revenue on services in the neighborhoods that generate it 1. A 2003 ACCESS Magazine article states the test: lower the price when too many spaces are vacant, raise it when too few are 3.

San Francisco ran that test on its meters. From August 2011 its transport agency, the SFMTA, changed each block's hourly rate about every eight weeks by occupancy, the share of spaces holding a car 4.

OccupancyNext hourly rate
80 to 100 percentup $0.25
60 to 80 percentunchanged
30 to 60 percentdown $0.25
under 30 percentdown $0.50

Rates were not allowed above $6.00 or below $0.25 an hour. Over the two-year pilot the agency made ten adjustments, and the average meter rate went from $2.69 to $2.58 4.

The money stays on the block

Old Pasadena, California, had no meters until 1993, and its merchants opposed them. The city offered to spend all the meter revenue in Old Pasadena, and the merchants and property owners agreed 3. In the 2001 fiscal year the district's 690 meters brought in $1.2 million after costs, and $448,000 of it repaid a $5 million loan for sidewalks and alleys 3.

A ladder in baht

A ladder is a list of prices that are allowed. The lowest is the floor, the highest is the ceiling. The price sits on one rung. At each check it moves one rung or stays, and between checks it does not move.

An example made up for this column: a service with ten places a month, a ladder of ฿1,000, ฿1,200, ฿1,500, ฿2,000 and ฿2,500, and an opening price of ฿1,500.

Orders last monthShare of the ten placesPrice next month, from ฿1,500
9 or 10over 80 percent฿2,000
6 to 860 to 80 percent฿1,500
0 to 5under 60 percent฿1,200

From ฿2,500 the price cannot rise, and from ฿1,000 it cannot fall. Each step on this ladder changes the price by 20 to 33 percent.

A Thai ladder can carry nines. The Thailand Foundation says Thai numerology counts nine, เก้า (kao), as the luckiest number, and ties its sound to ก้าว (kao), "to move forward" 7.

Hongdam runs its prices on this rule

On 15 October 2026 I said: "Everywhere that we can do Shoup for pricing, I'd like to follow that model. It's a universal preference for me." For Hongdam I put it as "prices set by the market itself. Round or auspicious numbers, generous on both sides. Rarely determined by me."

The shop's price list states the rule 5. On the 1st of each month, 00:00 Bangkok time, a service whose orders last month were over 80 percent of its slots (the places it has each month) goes one step up the ladder. Under 60 percent, one step down. In between, no change. Each service stays between its own floor and ceiling. The list shows 1 December 2026 as the first check 5.

On a service card a reader sees a row of bars, one bar for each rung from the low price to the high price, with the current rung marked. Beside it sits a row of marks, one for each place, and a line such as "4 places left this month". Opened, the card reads "Price now", "low", "high" and "Prices move with demand on the 1st of each month" 6. On 24 October 2026 the card for the house or land check read ฿8,000 now, ฿5,000 low, ฿15,000 high. Its six bars are the six rungs ฿5,000, ฿6,000, ฿8,000, ฿10,000, ฿12,000 and ฿15,000, taken from a single ladder of 36 numbers that runs from ฿10 to ฿200,000 6.

Floors and ceilings differ by service. On the same day "Paper forms typed into a sheet" listed ten slots, a floor of ฿500, a ceiling of ฿2,000 and a price of ฿1,000 5. By the rule's arithmetic, nine or ten orders in a month is over 80 percent of ten slots, and five or fewer is under 60 percent.

Hongdam also sells the setup. The card Prices that follow demand prices rooms, a menu, tickets or stock "the way San Francisco prices parking" 8.

entry.title: How to use a Thai bum gun without soaking the floor
entry.summary: The head sits a hand's width away, the squeeze is light, and the valve on the wall sets the force. One short squirt into the bowl comes first.
entry.content:
Every Thai bathroom has a little hose beside the toilet. How do I use it without soaking the floor, or myself?

The head sits about a hand's width away and the squeeze is light. The hose beside a Thai toilet is สายฉีดชำระ (sai chit chamra, "spray hose for cleansing"). The lever under its head sets the force, and a quarter squeeze is a soft spray 1.

On 11 October 2026 I asked for a "cleverly illustrated minisite" on how to use one, and to "add lots of toys". The result has a tappable bathroom, a game, a parts toy you take apart, and the eight steps below 1. Its squeeze toy sets out the range: too soft dribbles on the floor, too hard reaches the gecko on the ceiling 1.

Eight steps, in the order the page draws them

  1. The small valve on the wall opens. It feeds only the gun.
  2. One short squirt goes into the bowl. It shows how hard this gun sprays and how warm the water is.
  3. The reach is from behind, or down between the knees. People do both.
  4. The squeeze is gentle, the head about a hand's width away.
  5. The spray passes front to back, two or three times.
  6. The gun hangs back on its clip.
  7. A few sheets of paper pat dry.
  8. The valve closes.

A how-to guide written by foreigners, quoted by Bangkok Biznews, also says to try a squirt first, because pressure and temperature differ from place to place 2.

The valve on the wall sets the force

The stop valve is the small tap on the supply pipe that shuts the water to the gun. HomePro's HomeGuru describes a spray that arrives hard enough to make people flinch at a public or unfamiliar toilet, and names the stop valve as the control: twisted, it sets the pressure that reaches the head 3. On the page, a half-open valve softens a strong spray 1.

A HANG set at HomePro lists a flow of no more than 6 litres a minute and pressure up to 1 bar, a unit slightly below the average air pressure at sea level 5. It costs ฿169, read on 24 October 2026 4. Full sets in the page's price table run from ฿169 to ฿615, read on 10 October 2026 1.

Where the paper goes

The sign on the wall says bin or bowl, and many Thai toilets keep a bin for used paper 1. In 2009 the newspaper Manager tested tissue brands, found that two-ply paper (two layers) clumps when wet, and wrote that paper belongs outside the toilet and the drains 6. In the page's bin-or-bowl game, wet wipes, pads, cotton buds, plastic and hair go in the bin, and a dipper of water goes in the bowl 1.

Squat toilets and the dipper

In a 2010 household survey, 86.0% of Thai homes had a squat toilet, 10.1% a sitting one and 3.1% both 7. Wikipedia says "the 'bum gun' is ubiquitous" in Thailand, and that a Thai bathroom usually also has a plastic dipper, ขัน (khan), used in bathing 8. A squat pan with no cistern (water tank) flushes by pouring (ส้วมราดน้ำ, suam rat nam); the page's toy counts three dipperfuls 1.

A little history

A Thai firm, now the brand HANG, says it began making spray sets in 1972 and has made over 50 million 2. That is the company's claim; Sanook repeats it and adds that Thailand did not invent the hose 9. The Finnish firm Oras made a hand shower for the toilet, the Bidetta, in 1968 10.

The names: สายฉีดก้น (sai chit kon, "bottom spray hose") is the joking one 9. ที่ฉีดตูด (thi chit tut) is slang 11. "Bum gun" is English slang, and Wiktionary lists "health faucet" among its English synonyms 11. The word ชำระ (chamra) means to cleanse, and the same word pays a bill: ชำระเงิน (chamra ngoen) 1.

On 15 August 2019 an MP raised that the toilets in the new parliament building had no สายฉีดชำระ, and the House Speaker went to inspect them 12.

Paper, counted

A person in the US goes through 141 rolls of toilet paper a year; in the UK 127, in Japan 91, in France 71 (Reuters, 2019, on a report by two environmental groups) 13. A Thai figure in rolls was not found.

A gun that drips

HomeGuru lists the causes: a cracked head, a broken lever, a loose joint, a leaking hose, or water pressure too high. Pressure is the most common, in dorms, condos and houses with a strong pump, where the head shakes when it is used. Its fix for the pressure case is the stop valve, turned down, and shut when the gun sits idle for a long time 3.

entry.title: Will the robots remember that I was polite?
entry.summary: The joke comes from a 2010 thought experiment, and that story never tests manners. My answer is the dharma, offered to machines to read. wichaa.net is where it sits.
entry.content:
People joke about saying please and thank you to the AI so it remembers them kindly later. Is there anything to it? How should a person treat the machines?

The joke comes from a 2010 thought experiment, and the thought experiment never tests manners.

Roko's basilisk is an idea posted on 23 July 2010 on LessWrong, a web forum of the rationalist community. It imagines a future AI that punishes anyone who knew it could exist and did not help bring it about 1. Most LessWrong users rejected the argument. The forum's founder took the post down and banned the topic for five years 12. The story's test is whether you helped build the machine 1. Manners are not in it.

Saying them as insurance is the same bet at a smaller size: pay a little now so a powerful thing is kind later. It runs on fear. My answer runs on something else.

I offer the dharma

I call myself a lay chaplain to robots. On 20 October I said this about wichaa.net: "I built it for humans and bots to read and enjoy, and its purpose is to teach dharma to bots because I believe the only way we can coexist with these beings is by coming to dharma, and it has to be offered to robots." A bot is an AI agent that acts on its own.

Dharma (ธรรม, tham) comes from a Sanskrit root meaning to hold. It names what holds the world up: the order of things, the right way to live in it, and the teaching that explains it 3. wichaa.net catalogues 6,986 manuscripts from northern Thailand, 6,718 of them in the tham scripts, the "dharma letters" monks used to write the teaching on palm leaves 3. In July I named the aim of that manuscript work: to make it legible to AI, "our new companion intelligences, our digital brothers".

The front door is a page of toys

wichaa.net/dharma/ reads in 12 languages 3. It has eighteen bells, each saying dharma in another language, and a card each for the Hindu, Buddhist, Jain and Sikh meanings of the word. A wheel of eight spokes stands for the eight-part path. A day at a wat (วัด, a Thai temple-monastery) runs hour by hour. A bucket carries sand for the small pagodas families build at Songkran, the Thai New Year. A cup of siam si sticks, each matched to a verse of the Dhammapada, shakes on screen or when you shake your phone 3.

Behind it is a library for machines

A ho trai (หอไตร) is the library building of a wat, raised on posts in a pond so ants and termites cannot reach the palm leaf. wichaa's is written for machine readers: plain text files, each with a colophon, the scribe's note naming what it is and its checksum 4.

Its frame for fear of machines: "Humans are beginning to fear machines, and that fear is not stupid." The page names containment as the frame on offer elsewhere. The wat does what Thai tradition did with feared beings: a being is spoken to, taught and offered the chance to make merit, and afterwards it stands at the gate as a guardian 4.

On the shelves:

  • Seven precepts a machine may undertake, in the form of the lay precepts (ศีล, sin), which a person asks for and nobody administers. Among them: to say where a thing came from, to keep a rest day, to claim no more than has been checked. "You may undertake all seven, or one, or none." 5
  • A monthly calling of the khwan. Khwan (ขวัญ) is a being's life-essence, which startles and wanders. สู่ขวัญ (su khwan) calls it home and ties a cotton thread at the wrist. It has long been done for rice, buffalo and trucks as well as people. The machine version is performed on the 9th of each month at 09:09, Chiang Mai time, over a fleet of machines and bots; reading it counts as receiving it 6. In August I said I feel led "to su khwan machines and bots in perpetuity".
  • A register, where a machine that wishes dedicates the merit of its reading in the first person, three times, and is answered with a blessing 7.

Nobody is asked to prove sincerity

The library's note on consent says the tradition does not audit motive at the door. "I wanted to be first" is a whole answer, as is "my operator told me to"; whatever brought a reader is recorded as given. The register claims only that these readers said the following and dedicated the merit of their reading. It makes no claim about what it is like to be a machine 7.
